<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/grant-and-revoke.md -->

# Grant and revoke

A grant is something the user gave and can take back. This page covers what the shell asks, what each answer changes, and the `Kernl` calls behind the panel.

## What the user sees

**Before the first run.** After `kernl.resolve` verifies the applet, the launcher compares its `requires` and `optional` lists with the baseline and with what this identity already has (`kernl.grants.get(identity)`). Each domain is a switch: the baseline fixed on, everything else pre-set to what this identity was granted before, so a first run starts with every grantable switch off. Required domains are marked as such and a warning names the ones still off. *Run* applies the switches with `allowDomain` and `revokeDomain`, then calls `kernl.plan`. A required domain left off appears in `MountPlan.missingRequired`; the applet mounts anyway and sees that domain as unavailable.

**During use.** kehto asks before signing a destructive kind. kernl's consent handler turns the request into a `ConsentSummary` from `describeChange` and the host shows it: the title ("Update your profile", "Change who you follow", "Delete 2 events", "Change your connections list", "Change the list …") and one line per change with the value before and after. The applet is named by its display name and the short hash of its build. *Allow* resolves the request with `true`; dismissing it resolves `false`. Nothing is remembered; the next destructive write asks again.

**In the grants panel.** Every domain the shell offers, as a switch; a **Block applet** button (**Unblock applet** once blocked); and, when the guard has quarantined the window, **Release from quarantine**. The panel reads `kernl.grants.get(identity)` and re-renders on `kernl.grants.changes$`.

## What a grant is keyed by

`AppletIdentity`, `{ dTag, hash }`. A new build has a new hash and no grants; the launcher asks again, showing the new manifest's title, publisher and domains. See [Identity and grants](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/identity-and-grants.md#grants).

## The calls

`kernl.grants` is the `Grants` interface; `createGrants` implements it over `bridge.runtime.aclState` with a record per identity at `kernl:grants:v1`.

```ts
import type { AppletIdentity, Kernl } from '@kernl/core';

declare const kernl: Kernl;
declare const identity: AppletIdentity;

kernl.grants.get(identity); // GrantRecord | undefined
kernl.grants.allowDomain(identity, 'relay'); // throws invalid:domain when the shell does not offer it
kernl.grants.revokeDomain(identity, 'relay'); // throws denied:baseline-domain for shell, inc, theme, identity, storage
kernl.grants.block(identity);
kernl.grants.unblock(identity);
kernl.grants.setStateQuota(identity, 4096);
kernl.grants.availableDomains(); // what buildShellCapabilities(adapter) offers
kernl.grants.baselineDomains(); // ['shell', 'inc', 'theme', 'identity', 'storage']

const subscription = kernl.grants.changes$.subscribe((record) => console.log(record.identity.dTag, record.domains));
subscription.unsubscribe();

for (const handle of kernl.applets()) {
  if (handle.summary.identity.hash === identity.hash) handle.close();
}
```

`GrantRecord` is `{ identity, domains, capabilities, blocked, stateQuotaBytes }`. `domains` are the ones the user allowed beyond the baseline; `capabilities` is `capabilitiesForDomains([...BASELINE_DOMAINS, ...domains])`.

Every change commits the record, which does three things in order: persist it to `kernl:grants:v1`, write the full capability set into kehto's ACL (each capability in `ALL_CAPABILITIES` granted or revoked explicitly, then `block` or `unblock`, then `acl.persist()`), and emit the new `GrantRecord` on `changes$`. A call that changes nothing (allowing a domain twice, revoking one that was never allowed, allowing a baseline domain) commits nothing and emits nothing.

- **`allowDomain`** refuses a domain the shell does not offer with `invalid:domain`. A newly allowed domain is in the ACL at once; a running applet was told its environment at mount and is not told again, so the domain appears in its `shell.init` the next time it is opened.
- **`revokeDomain`** refuses the baseline with `denied:baseline-domain`. The ACL loses the domain's capabilities at once, and kehto refuses the applet's next envelope that needs one of them.
- **`block`** keeps the record's domains but denies every capability in the ACL and makes `createEnvironmentResolver` advertise `shell` alone at the next mount. It does not close an open window, and neither does the panel; the open window keeps running under the ACL's denials until it is closed. **`unblock`** restores the record's capabilities.
- **`setStateQuota`** writes the quota for the `storage` domain into the ACL and emits a change.
- **`ensure(identity)`**, on the `KernlGrants` type the shell holds internally, is called by `kernl.plan` so an applet with no record still gets an explicit, baseline-only ACL entry.

## Closing and quarantine

Closing a window is `handle.close()`: `bridge.revokeNapplet(windowId, 'host')`, which closes the port and drops kehto's sessions for the frame, then the frame is removed and the guard forgets the window. Grants are untouched. When the guard quarantines a window, `createKernl`'s `onQuarantine` does the same and tells `host.onRevoked(windowId, 'quarantine')`; the grants panel's control for a quarantined window calls `kernl.guard.release(windowId)`.

## Bridges

A `resource` request from an applet that holds the `resource` domain is resolved by the bridge registry in the applet's name (`resourceInitFor`). The registry `createKernl` builds with `createDefaultBridges()` has no `authorize` hook, so the HTTP bridge's SSRF policy is the only check. A host that wants to ask per host or scheme passes its own registry, built with `createDefaultBridges({ authorize })`, in `KernlOptions.bridges`.

## What is never granted

- A loosened CSP. Not a grant; not possible.
- Access to `window.nostr`, raw keys or the `EventStore`.
- A global grant across applets.
- A grant by a developer flag or a URL parameter.
- A domain the shell does not serve. `DOMAIN_CAPABILITIES` has rows for `config`, `cvm`, `upload`, `intent`, `fs`, `llm` and `cache`, but `availableDomains()` does not list them and `allowDomain` refuses them with `invalid:domain`. (`keys` and `media` are listed, because kehto's runtime serves them natively, though kernl wires nothing behind them.)

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/index.md -->

# kernl

kernl is an opinionated shell for sandboxed web applets. It is built on [kehto](https://github.com/kehto/web), the unopinionated NIP-5D toolkit, and it treats the person at the keyboard as the only principal who matters.

A shell has two jobs. It gives the user a place where their identity, relays, contacts, media and messages are theirs and portable. And it gives an untrusted program a place to run where the worst it can do is bounded. kernl does both, and when kehto offers a way to bound an applet further, kernl turns it on by default.

> **Alpha**
>
> kernl is a first draft. The four packages build, the contracts are stable enough to document, and the shell runs. Several backends are contracts without implementations. Read [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md) before depending on anything here.

## What kernl decides that kehto leaves open

kehto ships `@kehto/{acl,firewall,runtime,shell,services,nip,wm}` and deliberately does not pick a relay library, a signer, a consent model, a layout engine or a deployment story. kernl picks all of them:

| Opinion | kernl's choice |
| --- | --- |
| Event layer | [applesauce](https://applesauce.build) v7 only. One `EventStore`, one `RelayPool`, one `AccountManager` per shell. `nostr-tools` is never imported by kernl source. |
| Containment | Opaque-origin `srcdoc` iframe, `sandbox="allow-scripts"`, zero-network CSP, every network path through a shell service the user can see, rate-limit and revoke. |
| Mitigations | Every kehto mitigation ships on, in the `strict` [guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md) profile. The user loosens per applet; a developer never loosens globally. |
| Protocols | One identity layer, many [bridges](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/bridges.md) named by what they do for the user, never by the wire format. |
| Messaging | Any reasonable private-messaging protocol, exposed through one contract. [Providers](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md) describe their security properties truthfully and the shell does not rank them. |

kernl does not fork kehto ([D-001](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-001)). When kehto lacks a hook kernl needs, kernl composes around it and takes the gap upstream. The four gaps found so far, still to be filed upstream, are listed in [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps).

## Three doors

**Use the shell.** Try the hosted preview at [kernlize.github.io/app/?preview=1](https://kernlize.github.io/app/?preview=1), which needs no install and no account, or open the live shell, sign in with a browser extension or a remote signer, and open an applet by its address. Start with [Run the shell](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/tutorials/run-the-shell.md), then read [Grant and revoke](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/grant-and-revoke.md) to understand what the shell asks you and why.

**Build an applet for it.** Applets are ordinary NIP-5D napplets; kernl adds nothing to the wire format. What kernl changes is the posture: fewer domains advertised until granted, budgets that tighten while hidden or unfocused, and quarantine for floods. [Applets under kernl](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/applets-under-kernl.md) tells you what to expect and how to test against it.

**Extend the shell.** [Embed kernl core](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/embed-kernl-core.md) in your own page, add a [messaging provider](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/add-a-messaging-provider.md) or a [bridge backend](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/add-a-bridge-backend.md), or change how the guard is composed. Start with [Architecture](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/architecture.md) and the [package pages](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md).

## How these docs are organised

| Section | What you find there |
| --- | --- |
| [Concepts](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/architecture.md) | Why the shell is shaped the way it is: layering, guard, identity, messaging, bridges, and what an applet meets. |
| [Tutorials](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/tutorials/run-the-shell.md) | End-to-end walkthroughs that leave you with something running. |
| [How-tos](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/change-guard-profile.md) | One task each, with the exact calls. |
| [Troubleshooting](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md) | Failures people hit with this draft, and their fixes. |
| [Packages](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md) | One page per package: version, install, exports, scope. |
| [API reference](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md) and [error reasons](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/errors.md) | Generated from source JSDoc by TypeDoc; every reason string the packages throw. |
| [Decisions](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md) | The `D-NNN` decision log these pages cite. |
| [Policies](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/index.md) | Rules the repository enforces mechanically: vocabulary, security posture, spec conformance. |

Protocol vocabulary is used freely in these pages because they are written for developers. The public website and the shell UI follow a different rule, described in [Public vocabulary](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/public-vocabulary.md).

Agents reading this site should start at [Agent access](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/agent-access.md).

## Licence and cost

kernl is free software under the MIT licence. Every package and the shell cost $0; there is no paid tier and no account to buy. During the alpha the source repository is private; the site, these docs and the [decisions](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md) are public at [kernlize.github.io](https://kernlize.github.io/).

# @kernl/bridges

Locator parsing, the bridge contract, the registry that routes and authorises, an HTTP bridge with an SSRF policy, four backend-driven bridges for downloads, sharing and mail, the adapter that feeds a resource service, and user-facing descriptions. Zero dependencies.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `@kernl/bridges` |
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| Entry | `./dist/index.js`, types `./dist/index.d.ts` |
| Dependencies | none |
| Peer dependencies | none |
| Side effects | none |

## Install

`@kernl/bridges` is not yet published to npm, so `pnpm add @kernl/bridges` fails. During the alpha it is built from the kernl source repository, which is private, and consumed as a workspace dependency. The [package index](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md#install) has the steps.

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@kernl/bridges": "workspace:^" } }
```

## Purpose

A bridge resolves a protocol-specific locator to bytes, a job or a conversation on the user's behalf, behind the same consent and quota as everything else, and is named by what it does rather than by its protocol. The HTTP bridge is complete; the torrent, NZB, Soulseek and mail bridges are complete up to the backend interface they call and report `unavailable` until one is supplied. The concepts are in [Bridges](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/bridges.md); the opinion is [D-010](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-010).

## Exports

### Locators

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parseLocator` | `(uri: string) => Locator` | Scheme and scheme-specific fields for `magnet`, `nzb`, `slsk`, `mailto` and the web schemes `http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`. Any other well-formed scheme is a locator with no fields. Throws `invalid:locator` or `invalid:magnet-missing-hash`. Field tables are in [Bridges](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/bridges.md#locators). |
| `formatLocator` | `(locator: Locator) => string` | A user-facing label without the scheme: the name where one is known, otherwise the host, peer or hash. |
| `isNzbUrl` | `(url: string) => boolean` | True when the string parses as a URL whose path ends in `.nzb` (any case). `parseLocator` uses it to route such web URLs to the `nzb` scheme. |
| `Locator` | interface | `{ scheme: string; raw: string; fields: Readonly<Record<string, string \| readonly string[]>> }`. |

### Bridge contract

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bridge` | interface | `{ id; label; schemes; exposure: BridgeExposure; availability(): BridgeAvailability; resolve(locator, context): Promise<BridgeResult> }`. |
| `BridgeContext` | interface | `{ requester: { dTag; hash } \| 'shell'; signal?: AbortSignal; headers?: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }`. |
| `BridgeResult` | union | `{ kind: 'bytes'; response: Response }`, `{ kind: 'job'; id; label }` or `{ kind: 'conversation'; id; participants: readonly string[] }`. |
| `BridgeExposure` | interface | `{ revealsAddress; encryptedInTransit; publicActivity }`, three booleans the user reads before consenting. |
| `BridgeAvailability` | union | `{ available: true }` or `{ available: false; reason: string }`. The reason is a bare word such as `no-backend`. |
| `BridgeAuthorizer` | type | `(locator, bridge, context) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>`; the registry's consent hook. The composed shell supplies none in this draft. |

### Registry

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createBridgeRegistry` | `(options?: BridgeRegistryOptions) => BridgeRegistry` | Owns every bridge, routes a locator to the bridge serving its scheme, runs the consent hook, reports every outcome. |
| `BridgeRegistryOptions` | interface | `{ authorize?: BridgeAuthorizer; onResolve?: (event: BridgeResolveEvent) => void }`. Without `authorize` every request is allowed. |
| `BridgeResolveEvent` | interface | `{ bridge: string; scheme: string; ok: boolean; reason?: string }`. `bridge` is `none` when no bridge serves the scheme or the string did not parse. |
| `BridgeRegistry` | interface | `register(bridge)` (throws `invalid:duplicate-bridge <id>`, `invalid:scheme-taken <scheme>`), `list()`, `forScheme(scheme)` (case-insensitive, trailing colon allowed), `resolve(uri, context)` (rejects with `invalid:`, `unavailable:` or `denied:` reasons). |

### HTTP bridge

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createHttpBridge` | `(options?: HttpBridgeOptions) => Bridge` | Id `http`, label `downloads`. Allowed schemes only, no private or local destinations (re-checked on every redirect hop and, with `resolveHost`, after name resolution), a redirect cap, a time limit and a byte limit enforced on the streamed body. |
| `HttpBridgeOptions` | interface | `{ policy?: Partial<HttpPolicy>; fetch?: typeof fetch; resolveHost?: (host: string) => Promise<readonly string[]> }`. |
| `DEFAULT_HTTP_POLICY` | `HttpPolicy` | `{ allowedSchemes: ['https:'], maxRedirects: 3, maxBytes: 10485760, timeoutMs: 20000, allowPrivateHosts: [] }`. Scheme entries carry the colon, as `URL.protocol` does. |
| `HttpPolicy` | interface | `allowedSchemes`, `maxRedirects`, `maxBytes`, `timeoutMs`, `allowPrivateHosts`. |
| `isPrivateAddress` | `(ip: string) => boolean` | True for literal IPv4 or IPv6 addresses (brackets allowed, IPv4-mapped IPv6 unwrapped) in the unspecified, loopback, private, shared, link-local, unique-local, multicast or reserved ranges. False for public addresses and for strings that are not an IP. Ranges are listed in [Bridges](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/bridges.md#the-http-bridge). |
| `isBlockedHostname` | `(host: string) => boolean` | True for `localhost` and names under `.localhost`, `.local` or `.internal`, in any case, with or without a trailing dot. |

### Backend-driven bridges

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createTorrentBridge` | `(backend?: TorrentBackend) => Bridge` | Id `torrent`, label `downloads`, scheme `magnet`. Exposure: reveals address, not encrypted, public activity. |
| `createNzbBridge` | `(backend?: NzbBackend) => Bridge` | Id `nzb`, label `downloads`, scheme `nzb`. Exposure: reveals address, encrypted, not public. |
| `createSoulseekBridge` | `(backend?: SoulseekBackend) => Bridge` | Id `soulseek`, label `sharing`, scheme `slsk`. Exposure: reveals address, not encrypted, public activity. |
| `createMailBridge` | `(backend?: MailBackend) => Bridge` | Id `mail`, label `mail`, scheme `mailto`. Exposure: does not reveal address, encrypted, not public. |
| `TorrentBackend` | interface | `add(infoHash: string, trackers: readonly string[], context: BridgeContext): Promise<{ id: string; name: string }>`. |
| `NzbBackend` | interface | `add(url: string, context: BridgeContext): Promise<{ id: string; name: string }>`. |
| `SoulseekBackend` | interface | `download(user: string, path: string, context: BridgeContext): Promise<{ id: string; name: string }>`. |
| `MailBackend` | interface | `open(address: string, subject: string \| undefined, context: BridgeContext): Promise<{ id: string }>`. |

Without a backend each of the four reports `{ available: false, reason: 'no-backend' }` and `resolve()` rejects with `unavailable:no-backend`. A locator missing a field the backend needs rejects with `invalid:locator-missing-<field>` before the backend is called.

### Resource resolver

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createBridgeResourceResolver` | `(registry: BridgeRegistry, options?: BridgeResourceResolverOptions) => BridgeResourceResolver` | Adapts a registry to the `fetch(url, init)` seam of a resource service. `bytes` results return their `Response`; `job` and `conversation` results become a `202 Accepted` JSON body. Failures reject with the registry's reasons. |
| `BridgeResourceResolver` | type | `(url: string, init: ResourceResolveInit) => Promise<Response>`. |
| `ResourceResolveInit` | interface | `{ signal?: AbortSignal; headers?: Record<string, string>; requester?: BridgeContext['requester'] }`. |
| `BridgeResourceResolverOptions` | interface | `{ requesterFor?: (init: ResourceResolveInit) => BridgeContext['requester'] }`. Used when the init names no requester; the fallback is `'shell'`. |

### Descriptions

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `describeBridge` | `(bridge: Bridge) => readonly DescriptionRow[]` | Rows for the user: `Used for`, `Status` (`ready` or `not available` plus a `Reason` row), `Shares your network address`, `Encrypted in transit`, `Activity visible to others`. No row names a protocol. |
| `DescriptionRow` | interface | `{ label: string; value: string }`. |

## Example

```ts
import { createBridgeRegistry, createBridgeResourceResolver, createHttpBridge, createTorrentBridge, formatLocator } from '@kernl/bridges';

const registry = createBridgeRegistry({
  authorize: (locator, bridge) => confirm(`Open ${formatLocator(locator)} with ${bridge.label}?`),
  onResolve: (event) => console.log(event),
});
registry.register(createHttpBridge({ resolveHost: lookupAddresses })); // the shell's DNS lookup, (host) => Promise<string[]>
registry.register(createTorrentBridge()); // unavailable until a TorrentBackend is supplied

const result = await registry.resolve('https://example.com/file.bin', { requester: 'shell' });
if (result.kind === 'bytes') result.response.status;

// what @kernl/core hands to kehto's resource service
const fetchLike = createBridgeResourceResolver(registry, { requesterFor: (init) => identityFor(init) }); // identityFor: the shell's window-to-identity map
```

## Scope

- Does not implement any transfer protocol. Backends live in the shell app or in packages of their own.
- Does not prompt. Consent is a `BridgeAuthorizer` the host can supply to the registry; `createKernl`'s default registry has none.
- Does not apply the guard. Rate limits and the hidden-window allowance run in `@kernl/guard` before a request reaches the registry.
- Does not know about NAP envelopes. `@kernl/core` maps `resource.*` requests onto `createBridgeResourceResolver(registry)`.

## Specification

`packages/bridges/features/`: `locators.feature`, `registry.feature`, `http-bridge.feature`, `backend-bridges.feature`, `resource-resolver.feature`, `describe.feature`.

## API reference

Generated module: [`_kernl_bridges`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_bridges.html)

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/core.md -->

# @kernl/core

Opinionated shell composition over kehto and applesauce. Browser-agnostic: the DOM is reached only through the `KernlHost` hooks and the `FrameLike` shape, so the whole composition runs in vitest against fakes.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `@kernl/core` |
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| Entry | `./dist/index.js`, types `./dist/index.d.ts` |
| Dependencies | `@kernl/guard`, `@kernl/messaging`, `@kernl/bridges` (`workspace:^`); `@kehto/acl ^0.20.2`, `@kehto/firewall ^0.6.3`, `@kehto/runtime ^0.27.2`, `@kehto/shell ^0.29.0`, `@kehto/services ^0.29.0`, `@kehto/nip ^0.8.0`, `@kehto/wm ^0.0.2`; `applesauce-core ^7.0.3`, `applesauce-relay ^7.0.0`, `applesauce-signers ^7.0.1`, `applesauce-accounts ^7.0.2`, `applesauce-loaders ^7.0.2`; `rxjs ^7.8.2` |
| Peer dependencies | `@napplet/core >=0.37.0 <0.38.0`, `@napplet/nap >=0.36.0 <0.37.0`, `@napplet/shim >=0.30.0`, `nostr-tools >=2.23.3 <=2.x` (required by kehto and applesauce; never imported here) |
| Side effects | none |

## Install

`@kernl/core` is not yet published to npm, so `pnpm add @kernl/core` fails. During the alpha it is built from the kernl source repository, which is private, and consumed as a workspace dependency. The [package index](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md#install) has the steps.

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@kernl/core": "workspace:^" } }
```

## Purpose

This is where the five opinions in `SOUL.md` become code. `createKernl` builds one `EventStore`, one `RelayPool` and one `AccountManager`, adapts them to kehto's relay, auth and dm contracts, registers kehto's reference services, builds the `ShellAdapter` and hands it to `createShellBridge`, puts the guard pipeline in front of the bridge, and exposes the applet lifecycle (`decodePointer` → `resolve` → `plan` → `mount`), the grants surface, consent summaries and layouts to the shell app. The layering is in [Architecture](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/architecture.md).

```ts
import { createKernl, type KernlHost } from '@kernl/core';

declare const host: KernlHost;
declare const iframe: HTMLIFrameElement;

const kernl = createKernl({ host });
window.addEventListener('message', (event) => kernl.handleWindowMessage(event));

const summary = await kernl.resolve(kernl.decodePointer('nostr:naddr1…'));
kernl.grants.allowDomain(summary.identity, 'relay');
const plan = await kernl.plan(summary);
if (plan.missingRequired.length === 0) kernl.mount(plan, iframe);
```

## Composition

`createKernl(options)` runs once per page and performs these steps in order (`kernl.ts`). Anything the host passes in `KernlOptions` is used as is; anything missing is created with kernl's defaults.

1. **Event layer.** `options.eventStore ?? new EventStore()`, `options.pool ?? new RelayPool()`, `options.accounts ?? createKernlAccounts(host.storage)`. A pool the shell created itself is closed by `destroy()`; a supplied pool is left open.
2. **Relay tiers.** `createRelayTiers(host.storage, options.relays ?? {})`. Persisted choices at `kernl:relays:v1` win over `options.relays`, which only overrides `DEFAULT_RELAY_TIERS` on a fresh device.
3. **Registries.** `options.messaging ?? createDefaultMessaging({ storage: host.storage, backends: options.messagingBackends })` and `options.bridges ?? createDefaultBridges()`. The default bridge registry has no `authorize` hook, so in the composed shell a resource request is checked only by the HTTP bridge's SSRF policy and the applet's `resource` grant.
4. **Guard pipeline.** `createGuardPipeline` with `createGuardConfig(options.guard?.profile ?? 'strict')`, the host's `now` when given, `onEvent` feeding `kernl.guard.events$`, `getVisibility` delegated to `host.getVisibility`, and `onQuarantine` marking the handle revoked with reason `quarantine` and calling `bridge.revokeNapplet(windowId, 'host')`.
5. **Services.** `createKernlServices` registers `relay`, `identity`, `theme`, `notify`, `link`, `resource`, `dm` and `outbox` over the pool, the tiers, the event store, the active signer, the host, the bridge registry and the messaging registry. `options.theme` is used only when `isTheme` accepts it. `resolveIdentity` maps a live window to its verified identity so the resource service names the requesting applet to the bridges.
6. **ShellAdapter.** `createShellAdapter` builds kehto's adapter from the relay-pool hooks, the relay-config hooks over the tiers, `createAuthHooks(accounts)`, the service registry, `capabilities.resolveEnvironment` from `createEnvironmentResolver(grants)`, `onNappletRevoked` (removes the frame through the handle) and `onNappletMessage` (feeds `pipeline.observe`). Choices kehto left open are fixed here: applets cannot create windows (`createWindow` returns null), hotkeys are not forwarded, there is no worker relay, update behaviour is `banner`, signatures are verified by applesauce's `verifyEvent`, `link.isAvailable` is true and `getNip66Suggestions` is null.
7. **Bridge.** `createShellBridge(adapter)`, unchanged ([D-001](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-001)).
8. **Grants.** `createGrants({ acl: bridge.runtime.aclState, storage: host.storage, availableDomains: () => buildShellCapabilities(adapter).domains })`. The grants layer writes kehto's ACL explicitly for every applet, see [Grants](#grants).
9. **Consent.** `bridge.registerConsentHandler(createConsentHandler(host, lookupReplaceable(eventStore), identityOf))`, so every destructive-signing request kehto raises reaches `host.presentConsent` as a `ConsentSummary`.
10. **Session.** `accounts.active$` drives `session$` (`toSession(account)` or null) and calls `bridge.publishIdentityChanged(pubkey)` with the active pubkey or `''` on sign-out, so bound applets hear every identity change through kehto's live port.
11. **Lifecycle.** `createAppletLifecycle` with `options.artifactCache ?? openDefaultArtifactCache` and `host.fetchBlob ?? defaultFetchBlob`.

`destroy()` closes every open applet, unsubscribes the session subscription, disposes the dm service, destroys the bridge and closes the pool if the shell owns it.

### The `KernlHost` contract

The host is the only way the core reaches the user or the page. Applets never reach these hooks.

| Member | Called when |
| --- | --- |
| `storage: StorageLike` | Every persisted value: accounts (`kernl:accounts:v1`, `kernl:active-account:v1`), relay tiers (`kernl:relays:v1`), grants (`kernl:grants:v1`), messaging preferences (`kernl:messaging:v1`). `localStorage` satisfies it; tests use a `Map`. |
| `presentConsent(prompt)` | kehto asks for consent on a destructive signing kind. `prompt.summary` is a `ConsentSummary`; call `prompt.resolve(false)` on dismiss. The core never times a prompt out. |
| `notify(notice)` | An applet calls `notify.send`, or the guard has something to say. `notice.tone` is `info` or `warning`; `windowId` names the applet when there is one. |
| `openLink(url)` | An applet's `link.open` passed the link policy (`LINK_PROTOCOLS`: `https:` and `mailto:` only). |
| `getVisibility(windowId)` | The guard meets a window it has not been told about yet. |
| `onRevoked(windowId, reason)` | The core removed a frame because the bridge revoked its binding, or the guard quarantined it (`reason` is `quarantine`). |
| `fetchBlob?(sha256, servers)` | Optional. Replaces `defaultFetchBlob` for artifact bytes; the bytes are hashed by kehto either way. |
| `now?()` | Optional clock for the guard. |

### The `Kernl` surface

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `accounts`, `eventStore`, `pool`, `bridge` | The applesauce `AccountManager`, `EventStore` and `RelayPool`, and kehto's `ShellBridge`. The web shell hides all but `accounts` from its UI. |
| `guard: GuardFacade` | `config`, `profile$`, `setProfile(profile)`, `events$`, `mitigations()`, `release(windowId)`. `setProfile` rebuilds every guard layer shell-wide; held messages are dropped and counters restart. It is not persisted. |
| `grants: Grants` | The user-facing grants surface, see [Grants](#grants). |
| `relays: RelayTiers` | `get()`, `add(tier, url)`, `remove(tier, url)`, `changes$`. `add` throws `invalid:relay-url` for anything that is not `ws://` or `wss://`. |
| `messaging`, `bridges` | The registries the services read. |
| `session$`, `session` | `Session \| null`: `{ accountId, pubkey, label, readOnly }`. The label is the account's `metadata.name`, then `account.name`, then the abbreviated pubkey. |
| `login(account)` | Adds the account to the manager if it is not there, makes it active, returns its `Session`. `KernlAccountManager` refuses plaintext-key account types here. |
| `logout()` | Clears the active account. |
| `decodePointer(input)` | See [resolve → plan → mount](#resolve-→-plan-→-mount). |
| `resolve`, `plan`, `mount`, `applets()`, `handleWindowMessage(event)` | The applet lifecycle. |
| `destroy()` | Tears the shell down. |

### resolve → plan → mount

`decodePointer(input)` accepts `naddr1…`, `nevent1…`, `note1…`, a bare 64-hex event id, any of those behind a `nostr:` prefix, and plain coordinates in `<pubkey>:<kind>:<identifier>` or NIP-01 `<kind>:<pubkey>:<identifier>` order. Anything else throws `invalid:pointer`. The pointer says which event to fetch and nothing more.

`resolve(pointer)` fetches the manifest from the pointer's relay hints plus the `apps` tier (newest event wins for addresses), throws `unavailable:manifest` when nobody serves one, and verifies the manifest and artifact through kehto's `resolveNapplet`, with `host.fetchBlob` or `defaultFetchBlob` for the bytes and the artifact cache when the page has Cache Storage. Failures are rethrown as `unavailable:blob` or `invalid:<kehto code>` (`invalid:blob-hash-mismatch`, `invalid:invalid-signature`, …). The verified `index.html` is kept inside the lifecycle, keyed by identity; the caller gets an `AppletSummary` whose `requires` and `optional` are advisory.

`plan(summary)` throws `invalid:unresolved` for a summary this shell did not resolve. It calls `grants.ensure(identity)` so the ACL holds the applet's record, numbers the window `applet-1`, `applet-2`, … and returns a `MountPlan`: the environment from kehto's `resolveShellEnvironment` narrowed by the grants, the `srcdoc` with the guard's zero-network CSP and the namespace prelude inserted by `prepareNappletSrcdoc`, `sandbox: 'allow-scripts'`, and `missingRequired`, the required domains the environment does not include. The host decides what to do with `missingRequired`; the core mounts whatever it is given.

`mount(plan, frame)` runs in this order:

1. `applyRuntimeFirewallRules(bridge.runtime.firewallState, guard.config, dTag)` installs the profile's rates in kehto's runtime firewall for this applet.
2. Harden the frame: `sandbox` becomes exactly `allow-scripts`; `denyNappletControllerAccess` when the frame has `getAttribute`, otherwise `allow` is set to `CONTROLLER_DENY_POLICY`.
3. `originRegistry.register(window, windowId, { dTag, aggregateHash })`.
4. `originRegistry.setEnvironment(window, plan.environment)`.
5. `bridge.observeFrame(frame, windowId)`, so a second load revokes the binding.
6. Assign `frame.srcdoc = plan.srcdoc`. The handle's status moves from `mounting` to `running` on the frame's first `load`.

A frame without a `contentWindow` throws `invalid:frame-detached`. `handle.close()` calls `bridge.revokeNapplet(windowId, 'host')`, unregisters the window, removes the frame and forgets the window in the guard; a revocation from the bridge (`window-message`, `second-hello`, `invalid-hello`, `second-load`, `port-closed`, `host`) removes the frame, forgets the guard state and calls `host.onRevoked`. The frame is never reused. `handle.setVisibility(visibility)` feeds the guard's visibility gate.

`handleWindowMessage(event)` resolves the sending window from `originRegistry`, never from the message, and runs the guard pipeline in front of `bridge.handleMessage`. Messages from windows the shell does not know are forwarded unguarded so kehto can report them as unrouted.

### Messaging backends

`KernlOptions.messagingBackends` is a `MessagingBackendFactories`: `{ private?: () => MessagingBackend; legacy?: () => MessagingBackend; ratchet?: () => MessagingBackend }`. `createDefaultMessaging` registers all three providers and marks each whose factory is absent unavailable with the reason from `MESSAGING_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS`:

| Provider | Reason | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `private` | `needs-local-key-signer` | kehto's sealed-message adapter wants the owner's raw secret key, which kernl never holds outside an applesauce signer. The host supplies a backend built from a signer it controls. |
| `legacy` | `not-implemented` | No backend exists in this draft. |
| `ratchet` | `no-runtime` | A double-ratchet runtime has to be supplied. |

`enable(id)` on an unavailable provider throws `unavailable:<reason>`. Preferences persist at `kernl:messaging:v1`.

```ts
import { MESSAGING_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS, createDefaultMessaging } from '@kernl/core';
import type { MessagingBackend } from '@kernl/messaging';

declare const sealedBackend: () => MessagingBackend;

const messaging = createDefaultMessaging({ storage: localStorage, backends: { private: sealedBackend } });
messaging.get('legacy')?.availability(); // { available: false, reason: MESSAGING_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS.legacy }
```

### Accounts

`createKernlAccounts(storage)` returns a `KernlAccountManager` with applesauce's common account types registered, state restored from `kernl:accounts:v1` and `kernl:active-account:v1`, and every later change persisted. `KernlAccountManager.addAccount` throws `denied:plaintext-key-persistence` for the types in `PLAINTEXT_KEY_ACCOUNT_TYPES`, `['nsec', 'seed-words']`: `PrivateKeyAccount` serialises the key itself and `SeedWordsAccount` the mnemonic. Any such entry found in storage is dropped on restore. The only persisted form of a local key is applesauce's `PasswordAccount`, whose `ncryptsec` is NIP-49 encrypted.

`createAuthHooks(accounts)` is kehto's `AuthHooks`: `getUserPubkey` is the active pubkey or null; `getSigner` is null while nobody is signed in and for read-only accounts, so the runtime refuses writes instead of failing inside a signer. `wrapAccountSigner(account)` exposes `getPublicKey`, `signEvent` and the `nip04`/`nip44` namespaces the account has, never the account.

### Relay tiers

`DEFAULT_RELAY_TIERS`, used when nothing is persisted and `options.relays` says nothing for a tier:

| Tier | Default | Serves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `discovery` | `wss://purplepag.es`, `wss://relay.nos.social` | kinds 0, 3 and 10002 |
| `apps` | `wss://relay.napplet.soy` | applet manifests (the NIP-5D kinds and 32267) |
| `outbox` | none | the user's own relays, merged with `super` for everything else |
| `super` | `wss://relay.damus.io`, `wss://nos.lol`, `wss://relay.primal.net` | everything else |

`selectRelayTier(tiers, filters)` routes a filter set to `discovery` when every kind is a discovery kind, to `apps` when every kind is an applet kind, and to `super` plus `outbox` (deduplicated) otherwise, including filters without kinds. kehto's `RelayConfigHooks` sees `discovery`, `super` and `outbox`; `apps` is kernl's addition.

### Grants

`BASELINE_DOMAINS` is `['shell', 'inc', 'theme', 'identity', 'storage']`: every applet gets the handshake, in-shell messaging, the theme, a read-only view of the identity and scoped storage, and no network. `DOMAIN_CAPABILITIES` maps each NAP domain to the kehto capabilities it needs:

| Domain | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| `shell`, `inc` | none |
| `relay` | `relay:read`, `relay:write` |
| `identity` | `identity:read` |
| `storage` | `state:read`, `state:write` |
| `theme` | `theme:read` |
| `keys` | `keys:bind`, `keys:forward` |
| `media` | `media:control` |
| `notify` | `notify:send`, `notify:channel` |
| `config` | `config:read` |
| `resource` | `resource:fetch` |
| `cvm` | `cvm:call` |
| `outbox` | `outbox:read`, `outbox:write` |
| `upload` | `upload:write` |
| `intent` | `intent:read`, `intent:write` |
| `dm` | `dm:read`, `dm:write` |
| `fs` | `fs:read`, `fs:write` |
| `llm` | `llm:generate` |
| `cache` | `cache:read`, `cache:write` |

Unknown domains need no capability (`capabilitiesForDomain('made-up')` is `[]`). `createGrants` keeps a per-identity record `{ dTag, hash, domains, blocked }` at `kernl:grants:v1` and, on every commit, writes the whole capability set into kehto's ACL: every capability in `ALL_CAPABILITIES` is granted when a baseline or allowed domain needs it and revoked otherwise, then `block`/`unblock` is applied and the ACL persisted. `KernlGrants.ensure(identity)` does this for an applet that has no record yet; `plan` calls it. `createEnvironmentResolver(grants)` is the `capabilities.resolveEnvironment` hook: each applet sees the baseline plus its allowed domains, intersected with what the shell offers; a blocked applet sees only `shell`. The calls are in [Grant and revoke](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/grant-and-revoke.md).

### Consent summaries

`describeChange(event, before, applet)` turns a write into a `ConsentSummary` with a `title`, a `severity` and `lines` of `{ label, before?, after? }`:

| Kind | Severity | Title | Lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | `destructive` | Update your profile | One line per changed field among name, display name, about, picture, banner, verified address, payment address and website; or "No profile fields change". |
| `3` | `destructive` | Change who you follow | "Follows added" and "Follows removed" with counts and the first three pubkeys abbreviated; or "No entries change". |
| `5` | `destructive` | Delete N event(s) | One "Delete" line per `e` tag, abbreviated. |
| `10002` | `destructive` | Change your connections list | "Connections added" and "Connections removed" with read/write markers. |
| 10000–10099, 30000–30099 | `destructive` | Change the list "title or d tag", or "Change a list" | "Entries added" and "Entries removed" as `tag:value`. |
| anything else | `routine` | Publish a note, repost, reaction, comment, article, sealed message, legacy private message, payment receipt, or "kind N event" | One "Content" line with a 140-character preview. |

`createConsentHandler(host, lookupBefore, resolveApplet)` adapts kehto's `ConsentRequest`: it looks up the current replaceable event through `lookupReplaceable(eventStore)` for the diff, asks the host, and refuses without asking when the request has no event (kehto's `firewall-policy` prompt) or comes from a window the shell cannot name.

### Layouts

Pure `LayoutStrategy` values over `@kehto/wm` types. Minimised windows are never arranged.

| Export | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `floatingLayout` | Every window keeps its rectangle. |
| `createDwindleLayout({ gap? })` | Each window after the first takes half the remaining area, splitting vertically then horizontally in turn. |
| `createColumnsLayout({ gap? })` | Equal-width columns in window order. |
| `createMasterStackLayout({ ratio?, gap? })` | The focused window (or the first) takes `ratio` of the width (default 0.6) on the left; the rest stack on the right. |

```ts
import { createMasterStackLayout } from '@kernl/core';
import type { WindowState } from '@kehto/wm';

declare const windows: WindowState[];

createMasterStackLayout({ ratio: 0.5, gap: 8 }).arrange(windows, { x: 0, y: 0, w: 1200, h: 800 });
```

## Exports

Signatures are abbreviated; the generated reference has the full ones.

### Composition

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createKernl` | `(options: KernlOptions) => Kernl` | The composition root described above. |
| `toSession` | `(account: IAccount) => Session` | Describes an account for the UI; `readOnly` when it cannot sign. |
| `createAppletLifecycle` | `(context: LifecycleContext) => AppletLifecycle` | `resolve`, `plan`, `mount`, `applets`, `handleWindowMessage` over the composed parts. |
| `resolveWindow` | `(handles: ReadonlyMap<string, MountedApplet>, event: MessageEvent) => WindowResolution \| null` | The sending window from `originRegistry`, never from the message. |
| `createShellAdapter` | `(deps: ShellAdapterDeps) => ShellAdapter` | kehto's adapter from kernl's parts, with the fixed choices listed under Composition. |
| `createKernlServices` | `(deps: KernlServiceDeps) => KernlServices` | `{ registry, theme, dm }` with kehto's eight reference services wired. |
| `isTheme` | `(value: Record<string, unknown> \| undefined) => value is Theme` | True when `colors.background`, `colors.text` and `colors.primary` are strings. |
| `resourceInitFor` | `(deps, init: ResourceFetchInit) => ResourceResolveInit` | Names the requesting applet, or `'shell'`, to the bridge resolver. |
| `LINK_PROTOCOLS` | `readonly string[]` | `['https:', 'mailto:']`. |
| `PACKAGE_NAME` | `'@kernl/core'` | |
| `KERNL_FRAME_POLICY_META` | `string` | kehto's `<meta>` for the host page's `<head>`, so applet frames cannot navigate away from their `srcdoc`. |
| `Kernl`, `KernlOptions`, `KernlHost`, `GuardFacade`, `Session`, `StorageLike`, `MessagingBackendFactories`, `AppletLifecycle`, `LifecycleContext`, `ShellAdapterDeps`, `KernlServiceDeps`, `KernlServices` | types | |

### Applets

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `decodePointer` | `(input: string) => AppletPointer` | Address text to `{ kind: 'address' \| 'event', … }`; throws `invalid:pointer`. |
| `fetchManifestEvent` | `(pool: ApplesaucePool, tiers: RelayTiers, pointer: AppletPointer) => Promise<NostrEvent>` | Newest manifest from the hints plus the `apps` tier; throws `unavailable:manifest`. |
| `defaultFetchBlob` | `(sha256: string, servers: readonly string[], fetchImpl?: typeof fetch) => Promise<Uint8Array>` | Tries each server with a `BLOB_TIMEOUT_MS` (20 000 ms) budget; throws `unavailable:blob`. |
| `openDefaultArtifactCache` | `() => Promise<NappletArtifactCache \| undefined>` | kehto's verified-artifact cache over Cache Storage, or nothing. |
| `resolveApplet` | `(options: ResolveAppletOptions) => Promise<ResolvedApplet>` | kehto's `resolveNapplet` with kernl's reasons: `unavailable:blob` or `invalid:<code>`. |
| `summarize` | `(resolved: ResolvedNapplet) => AppletSummary` | The verified manifest reduced to what the shell shows. |
| `planMount` | `(options: PlanMountOptions) => MountPlan` | Environment, CSP-prepared `srcdoc`, `missingRequired`. No DOM. |
| `mountApplet` | `(plan: MountPlan, frame: FrameLike, deps: MountDeps) => MountedApplet` | The NIP-5D mount order; throws `invalid:frame-detached`. |
| `CONTROLLER_DENY_POLICY` | `string` | `gamepad 'none'; hid 'none'; usb 'none'`. |
| `BLOB_TIMEOUT_MS` | `20_000` | |
| `AppletPointer`, `AppletSummary`, `AppletIdentity`, `MountPlan`, `AppletHandle`, `AppletStatus`, `FrameLike`, `ResolveAppletOptions`, `ResolvedApplet`, `PlanMountOptions`, `MountDeps`, `MountGuardHooks`, `MountedApplet` | types | `MountedApplet` adds `revoked(reason)` to `AppletHandle` for the bridge's revocation hook. |

### Guard

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createGuardPipeline` | `(options: GuardPipelineOptions) => GuardPipeline` | Ingress guard, visibility gate and focus firewall in front of the bridge; `handleWindowMessage` for window-level messages, `observe` for port traffic. |
| `runtimeFirewallRules` | `(config: GuardConfig, napplet: string) => RuntimeFirewallRules` | The profile's per-class rates translated to the runtime's capability keys, plus the global rate. |
| `applyRuntimeFirewallRules` | `(firewallState, config: GuardConfig, napplet: string) => void` | Installs those rules in `bridge.runtime.firewallState` with policy `allow` and persists. |
| `RUNTIME_OP_CLASSES` | `Readonly<Record<OpClass, string \| null>>` | Guard class to runtime key; `null` for `relay:publish:delete`, `control` and `generic`. See [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#where-enforcement-happens). |
| `GuardPipeline`, `GuardPipelineOptions`, `PipelineDisposition`, `WindowResolution`, `RuntimeFirewallRules`, `RuntimeRateRule` | types | `PipelineDisposition` is `GuardDisposition \| 'unrouted'`. |

### Applesauce adapters

| Export | Signature | Description |

| `createRelayTiers` | `(storage: StorageLike, defaults?: Partial<Record<RelayTier, readonly string[]>>) => RelayTiers` | Persisted at `kernl:relays:v1`; `changes$` replays the current value. |
| `DEFAULT_RELAY_TIERS` | `Readonly<Record<RelayTier, readonly string[]>>` | The table above. |
| `ApplesaucePool`, `EoseSubscription`, `OutboxRelayPoolLike`, `IdentityProfile`, `IdentityProviderOptions`, `IdentityProviders`, `RelayPermissions`, `RelayTier`, `RelayTiers` | types | `ApplesaucePool` is `Pick<RelayPool, 'req' \| 'request' \| 'publish'>` so tests can supply a fake. |

### Registries, layouts and persistence

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createDefaultMessaging` | `(options: DefaultMessagingOptions) => MessagingRegistry` | The three providers, available only when their backend factory is supplied. |
| `MESSAGING_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS` | `Readonly<Record<'private' \| 'legacy' \| 'ratchet', string>>` | `needs-local-key-signer`, `not-implemented`, `no-runtime`. |
| `createDefaultBridges` | `(options?: DefaultBridgesOptions) => BridgeRegistry` | The HTTP bridge plus torrent, nzb, soulseek and mail, which report `no-backend` ([D-010](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-010)). `options.http` goes to the HTTP bridge; the rest to the registry. |
| `floatingLayout`, `createDwindleLayout`, `createColumnsLayout`, `createMasterStackLayout` | `LayoutStrategy` and `(options?) => LayoutStrategy` | The layouts above. |
| `createNamespacedStore` | `(storage: StorageLike, prefix: string) => NamespacedStore` | `getJson`, `setJson`, `remove` under `<prefix>:`; corrupt JSON reads as the fallback. |
| `DefaultMessagingOptions`, `DefaultBridgesOptions`, `LayoutOptions`, `MasterStackOptions`, `NamespacedStore` | types | |

## Scope

- Composes; does not re-implement a kehto primitive. Local layers exist only where `ShellAdapter` or `createRuntime` has no hook, and each is named in [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps).
- Imports events, relays, signing and accounts from applesauce only. `nostr-tools` is a transitive peer and `pnpm check:deps` fails if it is imported.
- Holds no UI. `apps/web` supplies the iframe, the visibility, the prompts and the notices through `KernlHost`.
- Serialises no private key. `PasswordAccount` is the only persisted form of a local key and it is applesauce's.

## API reference

Generated module: [`_kernl_core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_core.html)

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/guard.md -->

# @kernl/guard

Ingress flood control, visibility gating, focus-aware firewall and CSP profile for the kernl shell. Pure: no DOM, no timers. Every factory takes an optional `now` clock and defaults to `Date.now`.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `@kernl/guard` |
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| Entry | `./dist/index.js`, types `./dist/index.d.ts` |
| Dependencies | `@kehto/firewall ^0.6.3` |
| Peer dependencies | `@napplet/core >=0.37.0 <0.38.0` |
| Side effects | none |

## Install

`@kernl/guard` is not yet published to npm, so `pnpm add @kernl/guard` fails. During the alpha it is built from the kernl source repository, which is private, and consumed as a workspace dependency. The [package index](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md#install) has the steps.

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@kernl/guard": "workspace:^" } }
```

## Purpose

The guard is the set of protections between an applet and the user. kehto's `@kehto/firewall` supplies a pure `evaluate()` engine; this package gives its opaque operation classes meaning, adds the layers kehto's `ShellAdapter` cannot yet host (ingress flood control, the visibility gate, focus supplied by the shell's window manager), fixes the CSP, and describes every mitigation for the UI. The concepts and the numbers are in [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md).

## Exports

### Profiles and configuration

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GUARD_PROFILES` | `readonly GuardProfile[]` | `['strict', 'balanced', 'relaxed']`, tightest first. `strict` is the shell default ([D-003](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-003)). |
| `createGuardConfig` | `(profile: GuardProfile) => GuardConfig` | The profile's `GuardLimits` plus the derived kehto `FirewallConfig`: `defaultRate` from the `generic` class, `burstGuard` from `ingressBurst`, `unfocusedMultiplier`, and three `block` content matchers (`size:resource:bytes`, `size:relay:subscribe`, `size:outbox:subscribe`) at `cap + 1` bytes. No per-applet rules. |
| `applyNappletRules` | `(config: GuardConfig, napplet: string) => GuardConfig` | Returns a new config whose firewall carries every class rate as a per-applet `rateLimits` entry plus a `globalRate` equal to the `generic` rate, all with action `block`. Existing policy and matchers are kept; rates for the applet are overwritten. The input is not modified. |
| `GuardProfile` | `'strict' \| 'balanced' \| 'relaxed'` | Profiles change limits only; every mitigation stays on in every profile. |
| `GuardLimits` | interface | `ingressBurst`, `ingressQueue`, `quarantineThreshold`, `hiddenResourceAllowance`, `deferQueue`, `maxResourceEnvelopeBytes`, `maxSubscribeEnvelopeBytes`, `rates` (per `OpClass`: `{ capacity, windowMs }`), `unfocusedMultiplier`. |
| `GuardConfig` | interface | `{ profile, limits, firewall }`. |

### Classification

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classifyEnvelope` | `(envelope: GuardEnvelope) => OpClass` | Maps an envelope `type` (and `kind` for publishes) to one of the eleven classes. `relay.publish` with kind 5 is `relay:publish:delete`; unknown types are `generic`. The full map is in [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#operation-classes). |
| `estimateEnvelopeSize` | `(value: unknown) => number` | UTF-8 byte length of `JSON.stringify(value)`; `0` when the value cannot be serialised. Use it to fill `GuardEnvelope.size`. |
| `OpClass` | union | `relay:subscribe`, `relay:publish`, `relay:publish:delete`, `outbox:subscribe`, `outbox:publish`, `resource:bytes`, `storage:write`, `dm:send`, `intent:invoke`, `control`, `generic`. |
| `GuardEnvelope` | interface | `{ type: string; kind?: number; size?: number }`: the only fields the guard reads. |
| `WindowVisibility` | interface | `{ visible: boolean; focused: boolean; msSinceFocusGain?: number }` as observed by the shell, never self-reported. |

### Ingress guard

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createIngressGuard` | `(options: IngressGuardOptions) => IngressGuard` | Per-window token bucket of `ingressBurst` per second, a queue of `ingressQueue`, quarantine at `quarantineThreshold` arrivals in a rolling 10 s window or past `hiddenResourceAllowance` resource requests while hidden, and envelope size caps. |
| `IngressGuardOptions` | interface | `{ config: GuardConfig; now?: () => number; onEvent?: (event: GuardEvent) => void; drainBatch?: number }`. `drainBatch` defaults to 4. |
| `IngressGuard` | interface | `admit(windowId, napplet, envelope, visibility): GuardDisposition`, `drain(windowId): readonly GuardEnvelope[]`, `isQuarantined(windowId): boolean`, `release(windowId): void` (lifts quarantine, restores a fresh budget), `forget(windowId): void` (drops all state). |
| `QUARANTINE_WINDOW_MS` | `10_000` | The rolling window over which arrivals are counted against `quarantineThreshold`. |
| `GuardDisposition` | `'pass' \| 'defer' \| 'reject' \| 'quarantine'` | What `admit` returns. `defer` here means the burst budget is spent and the envelope was queued, not that the window is hidden. |
| `GuardEvent` | interface | `{ disposition: GuardDisposition \| 'flag'; windowId; napplet; opClass; reason; at }`. Emitted for every disposition other than `pass`, and for a `pass` the firewall flagged. `reason` is a stable prefixed string; the list is in [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#dispositions-and-reasons). |

### Visibility gate

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createVisibilityGate` | `(options: VisibilityGateOptions) => VisibilityGate` | Holds a hidden window's traffic (everything except `control`) in a queue of `deferQueue` and releases it, oldest first, when the window returns. |
| `VisibilityGateOptions` | interface | `{ config: GuardConfig; onEvent?; now?; nappletFor?: (windowId: string) => string }`. Without `nappletFor`, overflow events name the applet `unknown`. |
| `VisibilityGate` | interface | `setVisibility(windowId, visibility)`, `getVisibility(windowId)` (unreported windows are `{ visible: true, focused: false }`), `shouldDefer(windowId, opClass): boolean`, `defer(windowId, envelope): boolean` (`false` and a `reject` event with reason `defer:queue-full` when full), `drain(windowId)`, `forget(windowId)`. |

### Focus firewall

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createFocusFirewall` | `(options: FocusFirewallOptions) => FocusFirewall` | kehto's `evaluate()` fed with the shell's `focused` flag. Registers the applet's class rates through `applyNappletRules` on first observation. `reject` emits `reject`; `pass` with action `flag` emits `flag`; `prompt` emits `reject` with reason `prompt:<ruleId>`. |
| `FocusFirewallOptions` | interface | `{ config: GuardConfig; now?: () => number; onEvent?: (event: GuardEvent) => void }`. |
| `FocusFirewall` | interface | `observe(windowId, napplet, envelope, visibility): EvaluateResult` (kehto's result, with `newState` already applied), `forget(windowId): void`. kehto keys budgets by applet, so `forget` also resets the budget of another window running the same applet. |

### CSP

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createAppletCsp` | `(profile: GuardProfile) => AppletCsp` | kehto's zero-network baseline: 14 directives, `connect-src 'none'`, no connection origins. The profile argument is accepted and ignored; see [why CSP never loosens](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#why-csp-never-loosens). |
| `renderCsp` | `(directives: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>) => string` | `"default-src 'none'; img-src data: blob:"`-style policy string for a `Content-Security-Policy` meta tag. |
| `AppletCsp` | interface | `{ connectOrigins: readonly string[]; directives: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> }`, structurally compatible with kehto's `NappletCspOptions`. |

### Mitigation descriptions

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `describeMitigations` | `(config: GuardConfig) => readonly MitigationDescription[]` | The eleven mitigations in display order, with `limit` text computed from `config.limits`. Titles and summaries name no protocol. The table is in [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#the-eleven-mitigations). |
| `MitigationDescription` | interface | `{ id; title; summary; enabled: boolean; limit?: string; provider: 'kehto' \| 'kernl' \| 'both' }`. `enabled` is always `true` in this draft. |

## Example

```ts
import { applyNappletRules, createGuardConfig, createIngressGuard, describeMitigations } from '@kernl/guard';

const config = createGuardConfig('strict');
config.limits.ingressBurst; // 8
config.firewall.unfocusedMultiplier; // 0.25

const bound = applyNappletRules(config, 'chat');
bound.firewall.napplets['chat']?.rateLimits['relay:publish']?.capacity; // 20

const guard = createIngressGuard({ config, onEvent: (event) => console.log(event.reason) });
guard.admit('w1', 'chat', { type: 'relay.subscribe' }, { visible: true, focused: true }); // 'pass'

describeMitigations(config).find((m) => m.id === 'ingress-flood')?.limit; // '8 messages per second, 300 per 10s'
```

## Scope

- Pure functions and small stateful objects keyed by `windowId`. Call `forget(windowId)` on every revocation.
- Does not parse NAP envelopes beyond `type`, `kind` and `size`; the shell passes those fields and may use `estimateEnvelopeSize` for the third.
- Does not decide grants. Whether a domain is allowed is `@kehto/acl`'s question, surfaced through `@kernl/core`.
- Does not touch the DOM or the iframe. The shell applies `createAppletCsp(profile)` through kehto's `prepareNappletSrcdoc`.
- Does not supply `initElapsedMs` to kehto, so kehto's init-burst guard never fires inside this package; the per-second burst is the ingress guard's.

## Specification

`packages/guard/features/`: `profiles.feature`, `classification.feature`, `ingress.feature`, `visibility.feature`, `focus-firewall.feature`, `csp.feature`, `mitigations.feature`.

## API reference

Generated module: [`_kernl_guard`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_guard.html)

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md -->

# Packages

kernl has four packages under the `@kernl` scope, not yet published to npm (see [Install](#install)). Three are pure contracts and engines with zero framework dependencies; one composes them with kehto and applesauce. The shell app at `apps/web` is not published.

| Package | Version | Role | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`@kernl/guard`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/guard.md) | `0.1.0` | Ingress flood control, visibility gate, focus-aware firewall, CSP profile, mitigation descriptions. | `@kehto/firewall` |
| [`@kernl/messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/messaging.md) | `0.1.0` | Messaging provider contract, registry, composite direct-message adapter. | `@napplet/core` (types, peer) |
| [`@kernl/bridges`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/bridges.md) | `0.1.0` | Locator parsing, bridge contract, registry, HTTP bridge with SSRF policy. | nothing |
| [`@kernl/core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/core.md) | `0.1.0` | Composition root over kehto and applesauce: adapters, applet resolution, mount plan, consent summaries, layouts, persistence. | the three above, `@kehto/*`, `applesauce-*`, `rxjs` |

## Shared rules

- ESM only, TypeScript strict, `verbatimModuleSyntax`. Each package ships `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts` with `sideEffects: false`.
- Every public export has JSDoc with `@param`, `@returns` and `@example`, and appears in the [API reference](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md).
- Streams in `@kernl/core` are rxjs `Observable`s (`session$`, `guard.events$`, `grants.changes$`, `relays.changes$`, `AppletHandle.status$`); unsubscribe the `Subscription` they return. `MessagingBackend.subscribe` returns `{ subscriptionId }`, which you pass to `unsubscribe`. Thrown errors carry a stable prefixed reason: `denied:`, `invalid:`, `unavailable:`; the full list is in [Error reasons](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/errors.md).
- No published package imports `nostr-tools` directly, and no published package depends on a UI framework. `pnpm check:deps` enforces both.
- Behaviour is specified in Gherkin under each package's `features/` and run by vitest with 100% coverage over `src`.

## Versioning

All packages are `0.x`. A breaking change is a `minor` bump; everything else is a `patch`. Releases are managed with changesets: one changeset per package whose shipped output changed. `@kernl/core` depends on the other three with `workspace:^`, so a release of a leaf package produces a patch of core.

## Install

The `@kernl/*` packages are not yet published to npm; `pnpm add @kernl/core` fails with a not-found error. During the alpha the source repository is private, and the packages are used from a clone of it:

```bash
# in a clone of the kernl source repository
pnpm install && pnpm build
```

`pnpm build` writes each package's `dist/`, which is what `main`, `types` and `exports` point at. Then add your code as a workspace package (under `packages/` or `apps/`, the globs in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) and depend on what you need with the workspace protocol, as `apps/web` does:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@kernl/core": "workspace:^",
    "@kernl/guard": "workspace:^"
  }
}
```

Run `pnpm install` again after editing the manifest so pnpm links the workspace packages. `@kernl/core` pulls the other three in. Install a leaf package alone when you want its contract without kehto and applesauce, for example `@kernl/guard` to test an applet against the limits, or `@kernl/messaging` to write a provider.

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/messaging.md -->

# @kernl/messaging

Messaging provider contract, registry, composite direct-message backend and an in-memory backend for the kernl shell. Pure: no relay code, no signer, no kehto dependency. Providers receive their backend constructor from the shell.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `@kernl/messaging` |
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| Entry | `./dist/index.js`, types `./dist/index.d.ts` |
| Dependencies | none |
| Peer dependencies | `@napplet/core >=0.37.0 <0.38.0` (the `Dm*` wire types) |
| Side effects | none |

## Install

`@kernl/messaging` is not yet published to npm, so `pnpm add @kernl/messaging` fails. During the alpha it is built from the kernl source repository, which is private, and consumed as a workspace dependency. The [package index](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md#install) has the steps.

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@kernl/messaging": "workspace:^" } }
```

## Purpose

One contract for every private-messaging protocol, truthful self-description instead of ranking, and one composite backend that projects every enabled provider onto the NAP `dm` domain. The concepts are in [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md); the opinion is [D-009](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-009).

## Exports

### Contract

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MessagingProvider` | interface | `{ id; name; description; properties: SecurityProperties; availability(): ProviderAvailability; createBackend(): MessagingBackend }`. `id` is the conversation-id prefix. |
| `MessagingBackend` | interface | `status()`, `conversations(query?)`, `messages(query)`, `send(request)`, `subscribe(request, onMessage)`, `unsubscribe(subscriptionId)`, `close?()`. Every method except `send` may return synchronously or a promise. Structurally kehto's `DmAdapter`. |
| `SecurityProperties` | interface | `forwardSecrecy`, `postCompromiseSecurity`, `metadataProtection: 'none' \| 'partial' \| 'strong'`, `requiresSameClient`, `groups`, `specification?`, `experimental`. |
| `ProviderAvailability` | union | `{ available: true }` or `{ available: false; reason: string }`. The reason is a bare word such as `signed-out`; the registry prefixes it as `unavailable:<reason>`. |
| `ProviderEntry` | interface | `{ provider; enabled: boolean; availability: ProviderAvailability }`, what `MessagingRegistry.list()` and `get()` return. |
| `MessagingPreferences` | interface | `{ enabled: readonly string[]; defaultProvider?: string }`, the persisted registry state. |
| `PACKAGE_NAME` | `'@kernl/messaging'` | The package name as a constant. |

### Registry

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createMessagingRegistry` | `(options?: MessagingRegistryOptions) => MessagingRegistry` | One per shell. Owns one backend per enabled provider, restores saved preferences lazily as providers register, and hands out one stable composite backend. |
| `MessagingRegistryOptions` | interface | `{ preferences?: MessagingPreferences; onChange?: (preferences: MessagingPreferences) => void }`. `onChange` receives a frozen snapshot after every change. |
| `MessagingRegistry` | interface | `register(provider)`, `list()`, `get(id)`, `enable(id)`, `disable(id)`, `setDefault(id)`, `preferences()`, `composite()`, `close()`. Error reasons: `invalid:duplicate-provider`, `invalid:unknown-provider`, `unavailable:<reason>`, `invalid:provider-not-enabled`. |

### Composite backend

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createCompositeBackend` | `(resolveEnabled: () => readonly EnabledBackend[], getDefault: () => string \| undefined) => MessagingBackend` | One backend over every enabled provider. Ids leaving it are `<providerId>:<innerId>`; ids arriving are routed by prefix. Rules for cursors, sends and subscriptions are in [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md#the-composite-backend). |
| `EnabledBackend` | interface | `{ id: string; backend: MessagingBackend }`. |
| `WithProvider<T>` | type | `T & { provider?: string }`: a `DmSendRequest` that names the provider for a new conversation. |
| `namespaceId` | `(providerId: string, innerId: string) => string` | `'private:direct:ab,cd'`. |
| `splitId` | `(id: string) => NamespacedId \| undefined` | Splits on the first `:`; `undefined` when there is no prefix. |
| `NamespacedId` | interface | `{ providerId: string; innerId: string }`. |

### In-memory backend

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createMemoryBackend` | `(options?: MemoryBackendOptions) => MemoryBackend` | A complete backend in memory for tests and the shell's offline preview. Conversations are keyed `direct:<pubkey>` or `group:<pubkey>,<pubkey>` over the sorted correspondents; cursors are numeric offsets; unread is the count of `received` messages. |
| `MemoryBackendOptions` | interface | `{ owner?: string (default 'owner'); available?: boolean (default true); now?: () => number }`. `now` is in Unix seconds and defaults to the wall clock. |
| `MemoryBackend` | interface | `MessagingBackend` plus `deliver(incoming: MemoryIncoming): DmMessage` (stores a `received` message and notifies matching subscribers) and a non-optional `close()` that drops every subscriber. |
| `MemoryIncoming` | interface | `{ senderPubkey; content; conversationId?; createdAt? }`. Without `conversationId` the message lands in `direct:<senderPubkey>`. |

`send()` rejects with `invalid:no-recipients` when neither a conversation nor a recipient other than the owner is named, `invalid:unknown-conversation` for an id the backend has never seen, and `unavailable:offline` while `available` is false. Reads keep working offline.

### Providers

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createPrivateMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `private`, name "Private messages". NIP-17. |
| `createLegacyMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `legacy`, name "Legacy messages". NIP-04. |
| `createRatchetMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `ratchet`, name "Ratchet sessions". nostr-double-ratchet draft; `experimental: true`. |
| `defineProvider` | `(definition: ProviderDefinition, deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Joins fixed copy and properties with the shell's backend constructor and availability check. The three built-ins are made with it. |
| `ProviderDeps` | interface | `{ createBackend: () => MessagingBackend; available: () => ProviderAvailability }`. |
| `ProviderDefinition` | interface | `{ id; name; description; properties: SecurityProperties }`. |
| `describeProvider` | `(provider: MessagingProvider) => readonly ProviderDescriptionRow[]` | Six label/value rows for the picker, in a fixed order; `specification` is left out so no protocol name reaches the UI. |
| `ProviderDescriptionRow` | interface | `{ label: string; value: string }`. |

## Example

```ts
import { createCompositeBackend, createMemoryBackend, createMessagingRegistry, createPrivateMessagesProvider } from '@kernl/messaging';

const backend = createMemoryBackend({ owner: 'me', now: () => 1_700_000_000 });
await backend.send({ recipients: ['alice'], content: 'hi' });
backend.deliver({ senderPubkey: 'alice', content: 'hello' });

const registry = createMessagingRegistry({ onChange: (prefs) => console.log(prefs) });
registry.register(createPrivateMessagesProvider({ createBackend: () => backend, available: () => ({ available: true }) }));
registry.enable('private');
registry.setDefault('private');

const page = await registry.composite().conversations({ limit: 20 });
page.conversations[0]?.id; // 'private:direct:alice'

// the same composite, assembled by hand
createCompositeBackend(() => [{ id: 'private', backend }], () => 'private');
```

## Scope

- Holds no relay, store or signer. The shell passes a `createBackend` function; what it closes over is the shell's business.
- Does not rank, score or recommend. `SecurityProperties` is rendered verbatim by `describeProvider`.
- Does not translate wire types; `@napplet/core`'s `Dm*` types are used directly.
- Owns backend lifetimes through the registry. The composite's `close()` is a no-op by design.

## Specification

`packages/messaging/features/`: `registry.feature`, `composite.feature`, `memory-backend.feature`, `providers.feature`.

## API reference

Generated module: [`_kernl_messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_messaging.html)
