<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/index.md -->

# Policies

Rules the repository enforces mechanically. Each policy names the script that checks it and the decision in `DECISIONS.md` that motivates it. A policy that cannot be checked by a script is a convention, and conventions live in `AGENTS.md`, not here.

| Policy | Checked by | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Public vocabulary](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/public-vocabulary.md) | `pnpm check:vocabulary` (`scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs`) | [D-006](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-006) |
| [Security posture](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/security-posture.md) | `features/` scenarios, `pnpm check:deps`, Playwright in `pnpm test:e2e` | [D-001](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-001), [D-002](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-002), [D-003](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-003) |
| [Spec conformance](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md) | `features/` scenarios; review. Running `@napplet/conformance` in the suite is [roadmap](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/roadmap.md#_7-conformance) work. | `AGENTS.md` "Spec before code" |

Two further gates apply to everything, including these pages:

- **Docs gate.** `pnpm docs:check` builds TypeDoc and VitePress, then runs `scripts/audit-docs.mjs`: a page per package with its version row, every page in the sidebar, a TypeDoc module per package, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and a Markdown twin per built page.
- **Slop gate.** `pnpm slop` runs aislop over the repository and `scripts/assert-slop-score.mjs` fails below 100. Functions under 120 lines, files under 600, nesting under 4, at most 5 parameters, no narrative comments.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/public-vocabulary.md -->

# Public vocabulary

The public website and the shell UI never name a protocol. The person is the point; the protocol is plumbing. This page is the denylist, the reasoning, and where the rule stops.

## The rule

`scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs` scans the built output of `apps/web` (the landing pages and the shell's UI copy) and fails the build on any of these, case-insensitively, as whole words or prefixes where marked:

| Denied | Say instead |
| --- | --- |
| `nostr` | "your account", "the network" |
| `nip-` (prefix) | describe the behaviour: "signing extension", "remote signer", "private messages" |
| `napplet` | "applet" |
| `relay` | "network", or nothing: the user's relays are "where your account lives" |
| `pubkey` | "account", "address" |
| `npub` | "address" |
| `nsec` | "secret key", in the one place the shell must warn about it |

Two checks enforce it:

- **Build time.** `scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs` reads every HTML, Markdown, text, JSON and XML file in the Pages artifact outside `docs/`, so Astro pages, JSON-LD, `llms.txt` and the Markdown twins are covered.
- **In a browser.** `tests/e2e/public-vocabulary.spec.ts` loads every public page and walks the shell (sign-in, launcher, applet summary, a running applet's frame, the consent dialog with its record view open, and the guard, messages, grants and settings panels). It reads what a person can perceive: rendered text, `title`, `aria-label`, `placeholder` and `alt`. Copy rendered by scripts, which the file scan cannot see, is covered here.

Identifiers inside JavaScript bundles are not copy and are not checked. The consent dialog's record view shows every field of the event it will sign, with plain labels ("Signed by", "Type", "Labels") instead of wire field names.

## Why

Three reasons, in the order `SOUL.md` ranks them.

**The user's agency.** A person deciding whether to run an applet needs to know what it will do and what it can reach. A protocol name tells them nothing about either; it tells them which club they are supposed to already belong to. "This applet wants to publish on your behalf" is a decision a person can make. "This applet requires `relay` and `outbox`" is not.

**Protocol conformance is a property of the code, not the copy.** kernl conforms to NIP-5D and the NAPs, and the docs say so precisely. Saying so on the landing page would not make the code conform more; it would make the page about the specification instead of about what a person can do.

**Providers and bridges are chosen by what they do.** A user chooses a messaging provider by whether their correspondent can read it and what an observer learns, not by its wire format. A bridge is "downloads", not the name of a peer-to-peer protocol. Naming protocols in the UI would invite ranking by familiarity, which [D-009](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-009) and [D-010](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-010) rule out.

## Where the rule stops

- **These docs.** Written for developers, who need the names. Every page here uses them.
- **Code, specs, commit messages, issues.** `napplet` is the protocol term and stays in identifiers and in `features/`.
- **`specification` fields.** `SecurityProperties.specification` and a bridge's protocol are shown in the docs, never in the picker.
- **Addresses.** Server URLs a user adds, edits or removes are data, and their hostnames belong to whoever runs the server. Both checks ignore `http(s)://` and `ws(s)://` URLs.
- **The secret-key warning.** The one place the shell mentions `nsec` is the warning that it will never ask for one.

## The words we use

| Say | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| applet | napplet, app, dapp | "napplet" remains the protocol term in code and specs. |
| shell | OS, desktop, browser | kernl runs in a browser; it is not one. |
| grant | permission, capability | A grant is something the user gave and can take back. |
| provider | protocol | Users choose providers by what they do. |
| guard | firewall, mitigation | The guard is the set of protections between an applet and the user. |

Marketing adjectives, filler and hedges that hide a decision are out everywhere, including here.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/security-posture.md -->

# Security posture

The rules the shell keeps when it runs untrusted code next to the user's identity. Each rule has a scenario in `features/` or a check in `scripts/`; a rule with neither is a wish.

## Mount rules

1. **`srcdoc`, never `src`.** The applet document is the verified bytes with the shell prelude and CSP injected outside the signed content. A `src` URL would give the applet an origin and a network path the shell does not mediate.
2. **`sandbox="allow-scripts"` only.** Never `allow-same-origin`, never `allow-top-navigation`, never `allow-popups`. The frame has an opaque origin and cannot reach the shell's storage or DOM.
3. **The guard's CSP, unchanged by profile.** `createAppletCsp(profile)` is applied through `prepareNappletSrcdoc`; it returns the same policy for every profile. No grant, profile or setting alters it. See [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#why-csp-never-loosens).
4. **`denyNappletControllerAccess(frame)`** before the frame is attached, so the applet cannot reach a service worker or controller the shell registered.
5. **Order: register → set environment → observe frame → assign `srcdoc`.** `originRegistry.register(contentWindow, windowId, identity)`, then `originRegistry.setEnvironment(contentWindow, environment)`, then `bridge.observeFrame(frame, windowId)`, then `frame.srcdoc = plan.srcdoc`. Assigning `srcdoc` first would let the document's first message arrive before the shell knows who it is.
6. **Remove the iframe on every revocation reason.** `window-message`, `second-hello`, `invalid-hello`, `second-load`, `port-closed` and `host` all end with the frame gone and the guard's state for the window forgotten. A revoked window's identity is never re-bound to the same frame.

## Identity rules

7. **Verified bytes come from `@kehto/nip/5d` `resolveNapplet`.** Gateways and caches are accelerators; the hash is the identity. Cached bytes are re-verified on every read.
8. **Identity is `(dTag, artifactHash)` plus one port.** Grants are keyed by that identity; a new build is a new identity with no grants.
9. **Restrictive by narrowing.** `resolveEnvironment` returns only granted domains; kehto intersects, so the hook can only remove. The runtime's permissive default is never reached for an ungranted domain.

## Key rules

10. **Keys live only inside applesauce signer instances.** `ExtensionSigner`, `NostrConnectSigner`, `PasswordAccount`'s wrapped signer. kernl never holds raw key bytes and never serialises a private key outside `PasswordAccount`.
11. **Applets never see `window.nostr`.** The sandbox has no extension injection, and the shell does not forward one.
12. **Every signature the applet asks for goes through consent or an existing grant**, and destructive kinds (0, 3, 5, 10002) are shown as semantic diffs before signing.

## Network rules

13. **No applet network path exists outside the shell.** All bytes arrive through the `resource` domain and a bridge. The HTTP bridge enforces `https` only, 3 redirects, 10 MiB, 20 s and a private-address block re-checked on every hop.
14. **One `RelayPool`.** No service, provider or bridge opens its own connection. Adapters over the shared pool satisfy kehto's contracts.
15. **Hidden windows are deferred, not served.** The visibility gate holds their traffic; the hidden resource allowance caps their requests.

## Log rules

16. **Secrets never appear in logs, guard events or consent summaries.** `GuardEvent.reason` is a stable prefixed string; `NappletRevocation.detail` never includes message payloads; `describeChange` output names fields, not key material.
17. **Guard events are shown to the user**, with the applet and the reason. They are not sent anywhere.

## Dependency rules

18. **`nostr-tools` is never imported by kernl source.** It is a transitive peer of kehto and applesauce only.
19. **Published packages have zero framework dependencies.** `svelte`, `react`, `vue`, `preact`, `solid-js` and `lit` are forbidden in every `packages/*/package.json`.
20. **Leaf packages do not import `@kehto/*`**, except `@kernl/guard`, which imports `@kehto/firewall`. Only `@kernl/core` composes kehto.

Rules 18 to 20 are enforced by `scripts/check-dependency-rules.mjs` (`pnpm check:deps`). Rules 1 to 17 are scenarios in `packages/*/features/` and `features/`, and the mount rules are additionally exercised in the browser by the Playwright suite.

## Reporting

A posture violation is a bug of the highest severity in this repository, above any feature. Report it to the maintainers with the rule number; the source repository is private during the alpha. If it involves a kehto seam, the issue is filed upstream too, and `DECISIONS.md` records the gap.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md -->

# Spec conformance

kernl conforms to specifications it does not own. This page says which ones, what "upstream first" means in practice, and how a gap is recorded.

## Authority

| Area | Authority | Local copy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell–applet protocol | NIP-5D, [nostr-protocol/nips PR #2303](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/pull/2303) | none |
| NAP domains (`relay`, `outbox`, `dm`, `resource`, …) | [napplet/naps](https://github.com/napplet/naps) | none |
| Wire types and dispatch | [`@napplet/core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@napplet/core), pinned `>=0.37.0 <0.38.0` | the installed package |
| Shell composition | kehto source, `@kehto/*` at the pinned ranges | the installed packages |
| Event layer | applesauce v7, [applesauce.build](https://applesauce.build) | the installed packages |
| Messaging protocols | NIP-17, NIP-04, the nostr double-ratchet draft, as named in each provider's `specification` | none |

kernl keeps no local copy of a specification text. A copy drifts; a link does not. When the PR or a NAP document changes, the behaviour changes in kernl in a pull request that cites the clause.

## Upstream first

When kernl needs something a specification or an upstream package does not provide, the order is:

1. **Compose it from what exists.** Most of kernl is this: the guard composes `@kehto/firewall`'s `evaluate()`, the restrictive posture composes `resolveEnvironment` and `aclState.grant`.
2. **Propose it upstream.** An issue or pull request on `kehto/web`, `napplet/naps` or `nostr-protocol/nips`, as appropriate. The four kehto gaps kernl has found, still to be filed upstream, are listed in [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps).
3. **Implement it locally with a recorded gap.** Only when 1 is impossible and 2 is pending. The local implementation sits behind an interface, cites the upstream issue, and is removed when upstream lands.

kernl never re-implements a kehto primitive because it was easier than reading kehto's source, and never invents wire format. When a NAP is ambiguous, kernl prefers an upstream issue over a guess and records the ambiguity next to the code.

## What conformance is checked by

- **Gherkin scenarios** in `features/` for every protocol-visible behaviour, named after the clause they implement where one exists.
- **Review.** A change that touches an envelope shape, a domain's semantics or the handshake cites the clause in its description. A reviewer checks the clause, not the summary.

`@napplet/conformance` (envelope validators per NAP domain, manifest validation and the reference mock shell's expectations of a host) is not part of the test suite yet; running it against the shell's bridge is on the [Roadmap](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/roadmap.md#_7-conformance).

The docs are non-normative. Where a page here and the specification disagree, the specification wins and the page has a bug.

## Recording a gap

A gap is anything kernl does that the specification does not say, or does not do that the specification says. Record it in three places:

1. **Next to the code**, as a comment that names the clause and the upstream issue. This is one of the few comments the slop gate accepts, because a reader could not infer it.
2. **In `DECISIONS.md`**, as a `D-NNN` entry with Context, Decision, Consequences and Reversal cost. If the gap is a kehto seam, the entry says what upstream change would close it.
3. **In [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md)**, under upstream gaps, so a reader deciding whether to depend on kernl sees it without reading the decisions log.

A gap closes when upstream lands and the local layer is deleted. The `DECISIONS.md` entry stays, with a `Superseded by` line.

## Tie-breaking

Protocol conformance is second in `SOUL.md`'s tie-breakers, below the user's safety and agency and above the applet developer's ability to build. A conformance requirement that would weaken the user's position is not implemented silently; it is raised upstream with the conflict stated, and `DECISIONS.md` records which way kernl went while the question is open.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md -->

# API reference

The API reference is generated from source JSDoc by TypeDoc 0.28 with `entryPointStrategy: packages` over the four workspaces in `typedoc.json`. It is written to `docs/api/` and served next to this site at `/docs/api/`.

```bash
pnpm docs:api
```

Do not edit the generated files. Fix the JSDoc in `packages/*/src` and rerun. `treatWarningsAsErrors` is on, so an export without documentation or a broken `{@link}` fails the build. Source links come from `packageOptions.sourceLinkTemplate` and point at the source repository, which is private during the alpha, so they return 404 for public readers.

## Modules

| Package | Module page |
| --- | --- |
| `@kernl/guard` | [`_kernl_guard`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_guard.html) |
| `@kernl/messaging` | [`_kernl_messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_messaging.html) |
| `@kernl/bridges` | [`_kernl_bridges`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_bridges.html) |
| `@kernl/core` | [`_kernl_core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_core.html) |

The [index page](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/index.html) lists all four, and the [hierarchy page](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/hierarchy.html) shows type relationships across them.

## How to read it

- Each module page lists its exports by kind: interfaces, type aliases, functions, variables. Every entry has at least one `@example`.
- Reasons in thrown errors are documented as string literals (`denied:…`, `invalid:…`, `unavailable:…`) on the function that throws them.
- Types imported from `@kehto/*` or `@napplet/core` are linked to their names but not expanded; `excludeExternals` keeps the reference to kernl's own surface.
- The reference is HTML only. It has no Markdown twin and is not included in `llms-full.txt`; the [package pages](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md) carry the export lists in Markdown for agents.

## Audit

`scripts/audit-docs.mjs` asserts that `docs/api/modules/_kernl_<package>.html` exists for every `packages/*/package.json`, that each package page links to it, and that the built docs carry their Markdown twins. It also reads every built page and checks that each `href` into `api/` resolves, under `VITEPRESS_BASE` (default `/docs/`), to a file TypeDoc wrote; that is why the links on this page are relative (`../api/…`). It runs as part of `pnpm docs:check`.

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/errors.md -->

# Error reasons

Every failure in the four packages carries a stable reason string with a prefix that says what kind of failure it is. Code matches on the string; the UI maps it to words. This page lists each reason the packages throw or report, collected from `packages/*/src`.

| Prefix | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `denied:` | A policy or the user said no. Retrying the same request will not help. |
| `invalid:` | The input is malformed or names something that does not exist. |
| `unavailable:` | Something needed is missing or unreachable right now: a backend, a server, a provider. |

Thrown reasons are the `message` of an `Error`. A few carry a detail after a space (`denied:scheme http:`), so match on the part before the first space.

## Thrown errors

| Reason | Package | Thrown by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid:pointer` | `@kernl/core` | `decodePointer` | The input is not an `naddr`, `nevent`, `note`, 64-hex event id or coordinate. |
| `unavailable:manifest` | `@kernl/core` | `fetchManifestEvent`, so `Kernl.resolve` | No relay in the hints or the `apps` tier returned the manifest event. |
| `unavailable:blob` | `@kernl/core` | `defaultFetchBlob`, `resolveApplet` | No server returned the artifact bytes. kehto's `blob-unavailable` maps here. |
| `invalid:invalid-signature`, `invalid:invalid-manifest`, `invalid:aggregate-mismatch`, `invalid:blob-hash-mismatch`, `invalid:missing-index` | `@kernl/core` | `resolveApplet` | Verification failed. The part after `invalid:` is kehto's `NappletResolutionErrorCode`. Nothing runs. |
| `invalid:unresolved` | `@kernl/core` | `Kernl.plan` | The summary was not produced by this shell's `resolve`, so no verified bytes are held for it. |
| `denied:blocked` | `@kernl/core` | `Kernl.plan` | The user blocked this applet identity. |
| `invalid:frame-detached` | `@kernl/core` | `mountApplet`, so `Kernl.mount` | The frame has no `contentWindow`; it is not in the document. |
| `invalid:domain` | `@kernl/core` | `Grants.allowDomain` | The shell does not offer this domain in its current configuration. |
| `denied:baseline-domain` | `@kernl/core` | `Grants.revokeDomain` | Baseline domains (`shell`, `inc`, `theme`, `identity`, `storage`) cannot be revoked. |
| `denied:plaintext-key-persistence` | `@kernl/core` | `KernlAccountManager.addAccount` | The account type stores a raw secret key (`PLAINTEXT_KEY_ACCOUNT_TYPES`). |
| `invalid:relay-url` | `@kernl/core` | `RelayTiers.add` | The URL is not `ws://` or `wss://`. |
| `denied:read-only` | `@kernl/core` | the outbox service's signer | The session cannot sign, so an outbox publish is refused. |
| `unavailable:needs-local-key-signer`, `unavailable:not-implemented`, `unavailable:no-runtime` | `@kernl/core` | `createDefaultMessaging`'s `createBackend`; `MessagingRegistry.enable` | The host supplied no backend for `private`, `legacy` or `ratchet` (`MESSAGING_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS`). |
| `invalid:duplicate-provider` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.register` | A provider with this id is already registered. |
| `invalid:unknown-provider` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.enable`, `disable`; the composite backend | No provider has this id, or a namespaced id, cursor or `provider` hint names no enabled provider. |
| `unavailable:<reason>` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.enable` | The provider's `availability()` is false; `<reason>` is the bare word it reported. |
| `invalid:provider-not-enabled` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.setDefault` | Only an enabled provider can be the default. |
| `unavailable:no-default-provider` | `@kernl/messaging` | composite `send` | The request names no conversation and no provider, and there is no enabled default. |
| `invalid:no-recipients`, `invalid:unknown-conversation`, `unavailable:offline` | `@kernl/messaging` | `createMemoryBackend` `send` | No recipient besides the owner; a `conversationId` the backend does not hold; the backend was created with `available: false`. |
| `invalid:locator` | `@kernl/bridges` | `parseLocator` | Not a locator, or a malformed web, NZB, Soulseek or mail locator. |
| `invalid:magnet-missing-hash` | `@kernl/bridges` | `parseLocator` | A magnet without a `urn:btih:` hash. |
| `invalid:locator-missing-<field>` | `@kernl/bridges` | the torrent, NZB, Soulseek and mail bridges | The locator lacks `infoHash`, `url`, `user`, `path` or `address`. |
| `invalid:duplicate-bridge <id>`, `invalid:scheme-taken <scheme>` | `@kernl/bridges` | `BridgeRegistry.register` | A bridge with this id, or one serving this scheme, is already registered. |
| `unavailable:no-bridge` | `@kernl/bridges` | `BridgeRegistry.resolve` | No bridge serves the scheme. |
| `unavailable:no-backend` | `@kernl/bridges` | the four backend-driven bridges | The bridge was created without a backend. `availability().reason` is the bare `no-backend`. |
| `denied:bridge` | `@kernl/bridges` | `BridgeRegistry.resolve` | The registry's `authorize` hook returned false. The composed shell has none. |
| `denied:scheme <protocol>` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | The URL's scheme is not in `allowedSchemes`. |
| `denied:private-address <host>`, `denied:private-address <host> -> <ip>` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | The host is a blocked name or a private literal; the second form comes from a `resolveHost` result. |
| `denied:too-many-redirects` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | More than `maxRedirects` hops. |
| `invalid:redirect` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | A redirect without a usable `Location`. |
| `denied:too-large` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | `content-length` or the streamed body exceeds `maxBytes`. |
| `unavailable:timeout`, `unavailable:aborted`, `unavailable:network <message>` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | The time limit expired, the caller cancelled, or `fetch` failed for another reason. |

`@kernl/guard` throws nothing. Its decisions are events.

## Guard event reasons

The guard reports each non-pass decision as a `GuardEvent` with a `disposition` (`defer`, `reject`, `quarantine`, `flag`) and one of these reasons. They reach the user through `kernl.guard.events$` and the shell's guard panel. The numbers are per profile; see [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#profiles).

| Reason | Layer | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flood:burst` | ingress guard | More messages in one second than `ingressBurst` allows; the message is queued. |
| `flood:queue-full` | ingress guard | The ingress queue is full; the message is rejected. |
| `flood:quarantine` | ingress guard | Too many messages in the rolling window, or any message from a quarantined window. The applet is revoked. |
| `flood:hidden-resource` | ingress guard | A hidden window used up its `resource.*` allowance. The applet is quarantined and revoked. |
| `size:<class>` | ingress guard, focus firewall | The envelope is over the size cap for `resource:bytes`, `relay:subscribe` or `outbox:subscribe`. |
| `defer:queue-full` | visibility gate | The hidden window's deferral queue is full. Only the window-level `hello` passes through the gate ([D-012](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-012)). |
| `rate:<class>` | focus firewall | The operation class's token bucket is empty, for example `rate:relay:publish`. |
| `prompt:<ruleId>` | focus firewall | kehto's engine asked for a prompt; the guard treats it as a rejection. |

## Revocation reasons

`KernlHost.onRevoked(windowId, reason)` receives kehto's revocation reasons (`window-message`, `second-hello`, `invalid-hello`, `second-load`, `port-closed`, `host`) or `quarantine` when the guard quarantined the window. See [Architecture](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/architecture.md#the-mount-path).

## Related

- [API reference](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md): each function's JSDoc names the reasons it throws.
- [Troubleshooting](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md)

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/roadmap.md -->

# Roadmap

Ordered by the tie-breakers in `SOUL.md`: the user's safety and agency first, protocol conformance second, the applet developer's ability to build third. Nothing here is dated. An item moves off this page when its scenarios pass and its docs exist.

## 1. Upstream pull requests to kehto

None is filed yet. Each item shrinks kernl when it lands; see [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps).

- Forward `getFocusContext`, `onFirewallEvent` and `firewallPersistence` through `ShellAdapter` so the runtime's own firewall can be focus-aware without a second engine in front of it.
- Let the host choose the ACL default policy in `createRuntime`, so a restrictive shell does not have to write every capability explicitly.
- Offer a pre-dispatch hook on port traffic, so the visibility gate can hold a hidden applet's envelopes instead of observing them after dispatch.
- Expose a setter for the runtime firewall's `unfocusedMultiplier`, so the profile's focus tightening applies before dispatch as well as after.

## 2. Bridge backends

Each backend plugs into the path the HTTP bridge already exercises end to end. Order reflects how much of the user's exposure each one changes; see [Bridges](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/bridges.md).

| Backend | Interface | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mail | `MailBackend` | Opens or creates a conversation for a `mailto:` locator. Candidate for a shell-side IMAP/JMAP client or a hand-off to a configured mail account. |
| NZB | `NzbBackend` | Hands an `nzb:` locator to a configured downloader. The downloader runs outside the browser; the bridge reports job state. |
| Torrent | `TorrentBackend` | Adds an info hash with its trackers. WebTorrent in the shell, or a configured external client. Marked as public activity in the exposure description. |
| Soulseek | `SoulseekBackend` | Requests one file from one peer. Requires a daemon; the bridge reports job state. |

The shell also needs a downloads view that shows the state of each `job` result and lets the user cancel it; there is none today.

## 3. Messaging

- Supply the double-ratchet runtime so the `ratchet` provider reports `available`. Its properties are already described; see [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md).
- Per-conversation provider migration: move a correspondent from `legacy` to `private` when both clients can read it, shown as a reversible choice.

## 4. Mobile layouts

The window manager contracts come from `@kehto/wm`. A narrow-viewport layout with a window switcher, gestures for focus and dismissal, and the same visibility semantics the guard relies on (a window off screen is hidden, and hidden windows are deferred).

## 5. Account switching

`AccountManager` already holds several accounts. The missing piece is a switcher that makes the active account visible on every screen, keeps grants scoped to the account that gave them, and never signs a write with an account the user did not pick for that window.

## 6. Guard

- Per-applet guard profiles: today the profile is shell-wide and resets to `strict` on boot ([D-003](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-003)). Next: an override per applet identity, remembered locally.
- Re-narrow a live applet's advertised environment when a domain is revoked; today the ACL denies at once but `shell.init` only changes on the next open.
- Bridge consent per host: wire `createDefaultBridges({ authorize })` to a host prompt so a granted `resource` request still asks before reaching a new origin.
- Persist per-applet profile overrides and grants through a user-chosen sync, so loosening an applet once does not have to be repeated per device.

## 7. Conformance

- Run `@napplet/conformance` against the shell's bridge in `pnpm test`: envelope validators per NAP domain, manifest validation and the reference mock shell's expectations of a host. Today conformance is checked by the `features/` scenarios and review only ([Spec conformance](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md)).

## Not planned

- A global configuration flag that loosens a mitigation for every applet. `SOUL.md` opinion three rules it out.
- A second event library beside applesauce. `DECISIONS.md` [D-002](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-002) rules it out.
- A "recommended" messaging provider. [D-009](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-009) rules it out.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/tutorials/run-the-shell.md -->

# Run the shell

This tutorial takes you from nothing to an applet running in a window, signed in with your own account, and shows the `Kernl` calls behind each step. The hosted preview takes a minute and needs no install; running the shell from source takes about ten minutes and needs access to the source repository.

> **Alpha**
>
> The shell runs, but it is a first draft. Expect rough edges in the UI and read [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md) for what is not there yet.

## 0. Try it without installing anything

Open the hosted preview:

```
https://kernlize.github.io/app/?preview=1
```

The preview runs the same shell UI over an offline stand-in for the `Kernl` contract, with two sample applets and no network ([D-011](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-011)).

**You should now see** a card headed "Who is at the keyboard?" with a **Try the preview** button. Click it, then **Open an applet**; the launcher lists the sample applets *Notes* and *Pulse*, each with an **Open** button. Open one and click **Run**, and it appears in a window.

Without `?preview=1`, `https://kernlize.github.io/app/` is the live shell: everything below from step 3 on works there too, against real relays.

## Prerequisites for running from source

- Access to the kernl source repository. It is private during the alpha; the packages are not on npm either ([Packages](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md#install)). Without access, use the hosted shell above.
- Node 22 or newer and pnpm 10. The repository pins `pnpm@10.24.0` through `packageManager`; `corepack enable` picks it up.
- A way to sign: a browser extension that speaks NIP-07, a remote signer that speaks NIP-46, or nothing, in which case the shell creates a local account protected by a password. kernl never asks for a private key directly and never stores one in plaintext.
- The address of an applet to open, which you get from the applet's publisher (an `naddr1…` or `nevent1…` string, or a coordinate). The [napplet.run app store](https://napplet.run/apps/) lists published applets.

## 1. Clone, install and build

```bash
git clone <kernl source repository URL> kernl
cd kernl
pnpm install
pnpm build
```

`pnpm install` links the four workspace packages, the docs and the app. `pnpm build` compiles the packages into their `dist/` folders, which is what the app imports; skip it and the dev server cannot resolve `@kernl/…` ([Troubleshooting](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md#pnpm-site-dev-before-pnpm-build)). Nothing is downloaded at runtime later; the shell's CSP would not allow it.

**You should now see** `pnpm build` finish with a `dist/` folder in each of `packages/guard`, `packages/messaging`, `packages/bridges` and `packages/core`.

## 2. Start the site

```bash
pnpm site:dev
```

This runs the Astro dev server for `apps/web`. The landing site is at the root and the shell at `/app/`:

```
http://localhost:4321/app/
```

The first load shows the shell with no account. `boot.ts` has called `createKernl({ host })`, where `host` is the page's `KernlHost`: `localStorage`, the consent dialog, the notices, link confirmation and window visibility. The guard is already running in its `strict` profile and the relay tiers are `DEFAULT_RELAY_TIERS`. Add `?preview=1` to the URL to run the offline preview instead.

**You should now see** the sign-in card, "Who is at the keyboard?", with a list headed "Sign in another way". If instead a notice says "Running the preview" with "The live shell could not start (…)", the core failed to load; see [Troubleshooting](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md).

## 3. Sign in

Under "Sign in another way", pick one:

- **Use a browser extension** (button **Use**, shown only when an extension is present). The shell wraps the extension in an applesauce `ExtensionAccount`; your key stays in the extension.
- **Connect a remote signer** (button **Connect**). Paste a `bunker://` address into "Signer address" and click **Connect**, or click **Or pair from the signer** to get a pairing address for your signer app. Either way the shell holds a `NostrConnectAccount` over an applesauce `NostrConnectSigner` that talks through the shell's own `RelayPool`.
- **Read-only** (button **Choose**). Paste a public key into "Account id" and click **Continue**. The session is `readOnly`, applets see the identity, and every write is refused because `createAuthHooks` returns no signer.
- **Create a local account** (button **Create**). Choose a password, repeat it, and click **Create and sign in**. The shell generates a key inside an applesauce `PasswordSigner` and persists it as a `PasswordAccount`, whose serialised form is NIP-49 encrypted. A plaintext-key account is refused by `KernlAccountManager` with `denied:plaintext-key-persistence`.

Each path ends in `kernl.login(account)`, which adds the account to the `AccountManager` if it is new, makes it active and emits a `Session` on `kernl.session$`. Accounts and the active choice persist at `kernl:accounts:v1` and `kernl:active-account:v1`, so the next load lists the account under "Remembered accounts" with a **Sign in** button (a password account asks to be unlocked). Nothing is fetched at sign-in: profile, follows and relay list are loaded from the `discovery` tier the first time an applet or the shell asks for them.

```ts
import { createKernl, type KernlHost } from '@kernl/core';
import type { IAccount } from 'applesauce-accounts';

declare const host: KernlHost;
declare const account: IAccount;

const kernl = createKernl({ host, relays: { apps: ['wss://relay.napplet.soy'] } });

const session = await kernl.login(account);
session.readOnly; // true for a ReadonlyAccount; writes are then refused
```

**You should now see** the desktop: an **Open an applet** button, "Workspace 1 · 0 windows", "No applets open.", and on the right *Guard · strict · 0*, **Messages** and your account name, whose menu holds **Settings** and **Sign out**.

## 4. Open an applet by address

Click **Open an applet** (or press Alt+/), paste the address the applet's publisher gave you into "Applet address", and click **Look up**. `kernl.decodePointer` accepts an `naddr1…`, an `nevent1…` or `note1…`, a bare 64-hex event id, any of those behind `nostr:`, and a coordinate in either `<pubkey>:<kind>:<identifier>` or `<kind>:<pubkey>:<identifier>` order. Anything else is `invalid:pointer`, shown as "That does not look like an applet address."

`kernl.resolve(pointer)` fetches the manifest from the pointer's relay hints plus the `apps` tier, verifies its signature, fetches the artifact bytes by hash and verifies them. Nothing runs before verification passes; a tampered artifact is `invalid:blob-hash-mismatch`, a missing one `unavailable:blob`, a manifest nobody serves `unavailable:manifest`. When it passes, the launcher shows the `AppletSummary`: title, publisher, description, and under "What it may use" the domains it `requires` and lists as `optional`, each as a switch.

Baseline domains (`shell`, `inc`, `theme`, `identity`, `storage`) are marked "always on" and cannot be switched off. Every other switch starts where this identity's grants already are, which on a first run is off; a required domain is marked "the applet says it needs this", and while one is off the launcher warns "Without …, this applet may not work. You can still run it." Click **Run**. The launcher calls `kernl.grants.allowDomain` for each switch you turned on and `kernl.grants.revokeDomain` for each you turned off, then `kernl.plan(summary)`, and opens a window for the `MountPlan`. If `plan.missingRequired` is not empty, the applet sees those domains as unavailable.

```ts
declare const address: string; // from the applet's publisher

const summary = await kernl.resolve(kernl.decodePointer(address));
summary.requires; // advisory, never a grant
const plan = await kernl.plan(summary);
plan.missingRequired; // required domains the user has not allowed
```

The window's iframe is mounted with `kernl.mount(plan, iframe)`: the frame gets `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and the controller-denying `allow` policy, is registered with its verified identity, has its environment frozen, is watched for a second load, and only then receives `srcdoc`. The applet sends its `hello`, which passes through the guard pipeline on its way to kehto's bridge, and `shell.init` tells it the domains it has.

**You should now see** a window titled with the applet's name, with **Grants**, **Minimise** and **Close** in its title bar. It shows "Starting …" briefly, then the applet.

## 5. Watch the guard

The desktop bar shows *Guard · strict · N*, where N counts guard events this session. Click it to see the profile, the eleven protections with the limit each one applies in the current profile (`kernl.guard.mitigations()`), and "Recent events" (`kernl.guard.events$`). Each event is a sentence naming the applet, what happened and why, for example "Applet Notes was refused: too many publishes", which is the guard's `rate:relay:publish`. A quarantined applet has its binding revoked and its frame removed; the window shows "This applet was stopped." and a notice says so.

Changing the profile here calls `kernl.guard.setProfile(profile)`, which rebuilds the guard for every window and is not remembered across reloads. [Change the guard profile](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/change-guard-profile.md) has the details and the numbers.

**You should now see** the guard panel with `strict (default)` selected and, for a quiet applet, no events.

## 6. Grant, revoke, block

Each window's **Grants** button opens its grants panel. It lists every domain the shell offers (`kernl.grants.availableDomains()`) as a switch, with the baseline fixed on. Turning a switch on is `kernl.grants.allowDomain(identity, domain)`; off is `kernl.grants.revokeDomain(identity, domain)`. Both write kehto's ACL at once, so the applet's next call on a revoked domain is refused; the domains it was told about at mount do not change until it is opened again. Under "Standing", **Block applet** is `kernl.grants.block(identity)`: the ACL denies everything and the next mount advertises `shell` alone (**Unblock applet** reverses it). Closing the window is `handle.close()`, which revokes the binding and removes the frame; the grants stay, keyed by identity, for the next time you open the same build.

[Grant and revoke](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/grant-and-revoke.md) covers each call and what it changes.

**You should now see** the grants panel's "Standing" rows: the storage quota, "Blocked: no" and the number of guard events this window has had.

## Where next

- [Applets under kernl](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/applets-under-kernl.md) if you came here to test your own applet.
- [Embed kernl core](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/embed-kernl-core.md) to run the core in your own page instead of `apps/web`.
- [Deploy](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/deploy.md) to publish your own instance of the shell.
